phase6_critique.notes: R8 and R9 chased one defect class to the end of the chain: a funding gate resting on a number nothing in the plan collects. R8 found the search gate's numerator incomplete (the miss log had one writer, the table, so a question with no branch was never logged). R9 found the same gate still had no DENOMINATOR, because nothing counted answered questions either. The sorter now counts every question and logs the ones it has no branch for. R8 also caught an unverifiable claim about their internal refund approvals carried as a section heading; now hedged to what is published, with the assumption stated in our own voice and answered by the sheet. R9 promoted its own soft note to a failure after re-deriving it: the five-year cost row falls as the scenario improves and its training and upkeep drivers were unstated, so the row could not be checked. Now disclosed and verified against roi_drivers.json rather than copied from the critic's sentence. R9 also conceded it was wrong in R8 to nominate the no-show sentence as a donor after ringfencing it in R7.

seasonal_context: Mid-August. Alaska visitor season is in its last full month, cruise calls run into late September but seasonal staff start leaving from mid-August as college terms resume.
Federal fiscal year ends September 30, so federal contractors and 8(a) subsidiaries are in the Q4 obligation surge and their proposal load is at its annual peak.
Coho and silver salmon runs are on in Southcentral and Southeast; Bristol Bay sockeye is finished.
Alaska State Fair in Palmer runs late August into Labor Day.
Construction and field season closes in roughly six weeks, so permitting and closeout paperwork stacks up now.
Back-to-school mid-August drives a physicals and immunization surge through independent clinics.
